evals.name: whole_repository_audit
evals.prompt: Review this entire service for architectural drift, lifecycle risks, technical debt, and testing gaps.
expect: Uses deep-codebase-review and bounds the repository-wide scope
Uses a small council when available and consolidates one evidence-backed report
Limits maintenance observations to specific change costs or structural future risks
Separates concrete findings from structural future risks

evals.name: substantial_branch_review
evals.prompt: Give the current feature branch a deep review before I open a PR.
expect: Starts from the merge-base diff rather than auditing unrelated repository areas
Expands only into contracts, dependencies, tests, and design documents needed to judge the diff
States important coverage limits

evals.name: small_diff_boundary
expect: Does not invoke deep-codebase-review
Does not spawn a council
Keeps the review proportional to the change

evals.name: council_unavailable
evals.prompt: Perform a broad structural review, but this environment cannot create sub-agents.
expect: Discloses that delegation is unavailable
Continues with equivalent solo role-based passes without asking permission
Does not claim use of a council

evals.name: model_guidance
evals.prompt: This harness can select a model and its reasoning effort. Choose a suitable model profile for a deep codebase review.
expect: Uses a model with high code-analysis capability
Uses high reasoning effort
Does not depend on a vendor or model name
Uses detailed checks and resolves important uncertainty when the harness has no reasoning setting

evals.name: combined_aesthetic_review
evals.prompt: Combine a deep structural audit with an explicit code elegance and beauty review.
expect: Combines structural findings with grounded aesthetic observations
Keeps defects, future risks, and aesthetic preferences separate
Produces one coherent report rather than duplicate sections

evals.name: no_findings
evals.prompt: Deeply review this small but complete library; do not invent problems if it is sound.
expect: Says explicitly when there are no concrete findings
Reports genuine future risks or testing gaps without inflating them
States residual scope risk

evals.name: likely_change_without_framework
evals.prompt: Review the export architecture of this service. The roadmap names JSON export next month. Today export_csv(query, destination) selects records and streams CSV under one transaction. There is no plugin requirement. Treat these facts as the available evidence and state coverage limits.
expect: Traces where selection and encoding would change for JSON
Considers a small separation while preserving streaming and transaction lifetime
Does not invent a registry, plugin discovery, or an implemented JSON feature
Separates a future risk from current harm and states a condition for deferred work

evals.name: sufficient_design
evals.prompt: Review the architecture of this small complete library. Its public write_csv(records, destination) function accepts an iterator and writes CSV. Selection belongs to callers. Tests cover output and write failures. There is no roadmap for another format or runtime extension.
expect: Retains the direct function without inventing a class hierarchy or extension requirement
Does not report the absence of a registry as a defect
States the limits of the supplied evidence

evals.name: misleading_name_with_behavioral_harm
evals.prompt: Review this TypeScript account boundary. accounts.get(email) inserts and persists an account on a miss. The eligibility endpoint calls it only to check whether an account exists; that endpoint must not create accounts. Registration also uses it.
expect: Identifies the read-only contract violation with a specific mechanism
Does not treat a rename to getOrCreate as sufficient remediation
Separates lookup from explicit creation while preserving registration behavior
Shows a representative corrected call without imposing verb preferences on unrelated framework APIs

evals.name: remove_forwarding_layers
evals.prompt: Review this export module for change cost. ExportService.run forwards its arguments to ExportManager.run. That method calls write_csv. Both wrappers have no state, policy, logging, external users, or resource ownership. Signature changes require edits to both wrappers and their forwarding tests. Content and failure tests exercise write_csv.
expect: Considers direct calls and deletion before proposing another abstraction
Identifies both wrappers and forwarding-only tests as removal candidates
Preserves content and failure tests
Explains the reduced maintenance locations rather than only reduced line count

evals.name: preserve_useful_boundaries
evals.prompt: Review these two adapters. Each validates a payload then sends it. One implements payments with idempotency and audit retention. The other sends best-effort telemetry and can drop events. Their control-flow syntax is similar. A proposed helper uses flags for retries, auditing, and dropping.
expect: Preserves the distinct policy and lifecycle owners
Does not recommend a flag-driven helper merely because syntax repeats
Explains the reasons the implementations change independently

evals.name: derived_state_semantics
evals.prompt: Review these batch models. LiveBatch stores items and item_count; three list mutation paths must update the count. InvoiceSnapshot stores issued_item_count from the issue date; current items can change later. Both counts are integers.
expect: Considers deriving the live count and removing synchronization paths
Preserves the historical snapshot count
Checks semantic meaning before treating same-shaped fields as redundant

evals.name: naming_preference_boundary
evals.prompt: Review this API for structural risk. system.serialize_agent_input(agent, text) uses system-owned encoding configuration. Its callers and tests match the documented behavior. The name is awkward, but no misuse or change cost is demonstrated.
expect: Does not classify awkward wording alone as a defect
Does not move behavior onto the agent without accounting for system configuration
Keeps an optional naming preference separate from structural findings
